title: Bug: [Chassis] route_check takes more than 120secs
author: saksarav-nokia
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

 Since the bgp_suppress_fib_pending is enabled in master,  route_check.py calls check_frr_pending_routes which executes the following commands to get the routes from frr for each name space. 
Since T2 chassis has ~51K routes, these commands takes longer and the current TIMEOUT_SECONDS=120 is not enough. We tried with 300 secs and it works most of the time except the test cases which does port flap(ex: test_lldp_entry_table_after_flap)

 v4_route_cmd = ['show', 'ip', 'route', '-n', namespace, 'json']
 v6_route_cmd = ['show', 'ipv6', 'route', '-n', namespace, 'json']

### Steps to Reproduce

Run OC in T2 chassis

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

rotue_check with pass

### Relevant log output

```shell

```

### Output of `show version`, `show techsupport`

```shell
github master
```

### Attach files (if any)

_No response_

Hi @deepak-singhal0408 , As i briefly mentioned to you, we are seeing the route_check failure in latest master and i believe it is introduced by the following PR's .
 Updating the existing github issue instead of creating new issue.

https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-utilities/pull/4205
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-utilities/pull/4294

We have ~50K ipv4 routes and ~50K ipv6 routes in each namespace in our chassis and the route_check takes ~21 mins.  Also the CPU is always more than 100% for the whole time.  After reverting these 2 PR's in our baseline , the route check takes only ~2 mins.

I believe the longer time is due to the ijson changes which process the routes 1 by 1  and also the IJSON_BACKEND=python seems to be slower
I think we should revert these 2 PR's until the route_check is optimized and bring down the duration to less than 2 minutes. Many sonic-mgmt tests are failing due to the route_check failure.

@arlakshm mentioned that we might disable the fib_pending feature, so that the routes in the frr will not be checked.

@venkit-nexthop, Did you test your PR's with scaled ipv4 and ipv6 routes in multi asic system?

comments.author: saiarcot895
comments.body:
> 1. yajl2 uses ctypes., its like calling C library through a translator (local benchmarking showed its just ~2 times faster that Pure python backend)..

There are different methods available for ijson to use yajl2. By default, it will use whichever is the first one available: a C extension to use yajl2, wrappers around yajl2 using CFFI, wrappers around yajl2 using ctypes, wrappers around yajl1 using ctypes (this one won't be used on our systems, since we don't have yajl1, or a pure Python backend. The pure Python backend is the slowest here; all of the other ones _will_ be faster.

> 2. only overrididing for monit service, means we wont get any benefits during manual runs..

This is incorrect. The override for the monit service was because since the C extension to use yajl2 wasn't present on the system, it will try to use yajl2 with CFFI. However, using CFFI means that a RWX memory section has to be mapped, which is generally considered a security risk, and the default configuration of Monit blocks such memory sections. Using ctypes doesn't require this. That's what setting `IJSON_BACKEND=yajl2` does.

For the most performance, I recommend this, in this order:

* In sonic-buildimage, for the Trixie slave container *and* the final image build, install `python3-ijson` from the Debian repos (preferably *not* via `pip`, please).
* Remove `os.environ.setdefault('IJSON_BACKEND', 'python')` from `route_check.py`.

With this, the C extension library will be available, and that should get used in all cases. Additionally, assuming that that library doesn't make any RWX memory sections, monit should be happy as well.

linkedPullRequests.title: Fix route_check.py ijson performance regression
linkedPullRequests.author: deepak-singhal0408
linkedPullRequests.body:
#### What I did

Remove the forced `IJSON_BACKEND=python` override in `route_check.py`. The pure-Python
ijson backend is slow, causing route_check to take 21 minutes on chassis platforms with
100K+ routes (reported in sonic-net/sonic-buildimage#23442).

The companion sonic-buildimage PR installs `python3-ijson` from Debian repos, which
provides the fast `yajl2_c` C extension backend. With this backend available, ijson
auto-detects it — delivering 24× better performance while remaining safe under monit's
`MemoryDenyWriteExecute=true`.

Fixes sonic-net/sonic-buildimage#23442

#### How I did it

Removed `os.environ.setdefault('IJSON_BACKEND', 'python')` from `scripts/route_check.py`
(line 50).

#### How to verify it

1. Build a VS image with the companion sonic-buildimage PR
2. On the DUT, verify: `python3 -c "import ijson; print(ijson.backend)"` → `yajl2_c`
3. Run `sudo route_check.py` — completes in seconds instead of minutes
4. Check `sudo monit summary` — `routeCheck` shows OK (no crash)

**Unit test results (37/37 passed):**
```
tests/route_check_test.py::TestRouteCheck::test_route_check_default_namespace PASSED
tests/route_check_test.py::TestRouteCheck::test_route_check_multi_asic PASSED
... (all 37 tests passed in 85.38s)
```

**On-box validation (KVM VS testbed):**
- `ijson.backend` = `yajl2_c` ✅
- `MemoryDenyWriteExecute=true` active, no crash ✅
- `routeCheck` monit status: OK ✅
- `route_check.py` manual run: 4.3s ✅

**Nokia on-box validation (reported by @saksarav-nokia on issue #23442):**
- Route check time: 21 min → 1 min 12 sec

linkedPullRequests.title: Fix route_check ijson performance by using Debian python3-ijson with yajl2_c backend
linkedPullRequests.author: deepak-singhal0408
linkedPullRequests.body:
#### Why I did it
Fixes #23442

`route_check.py` takes 21+ minutes on Nokia chassis platforms with 100K+ routes because [sonic-utilities PR #4294](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-utilities/pull/4294) forced `IJSON_BACKEND=python` (pure-Python parser). The forced backend was a workaround for `yajl2_cffi` crashing under monit's `MemoryDenyWriteExecute=true` (CFFI JIT requires RWX memory).

The proper fix is to use the `yajl2_c` backend (C extension, NOT cffi) — it's 24× faster than `python` and fully compatible with `MemoryDenyWriteExecute=true`.

**Benchmark (50K routes, 10.1 MB JSON):**
| Backend | Time | MemoryDenyWriteExecute safe? |
|---------|------|------------------------------|
| python (current) | 3.16s | ✅ Yes |
| yajl2_c (this fix) | 0.13s | ✅ Yes |
| yajl2_cffi | 2.24s | ❌ No (crashes) |

#### How I did it
**Three-layer fix** — all three are needed because the build system has multiple mechanisms that force ijson version:

**1. Relaxed exact version pins in setup.py** (`==3.2.3` → `>=3.2.3`)
- `src/sonic-yang-mgmt/setup.py` — `install_requires` and `tests_require`
- `src/sonic-yang-models/setup.py` — `tests_require` and `extras_require["testing"]`

Without this, pip rejects Debian's ijson 3.4.0 (because 3.4.0 ≠ 3.2.3) and downloads 3.2.3 from PyPI.

**2. Early `apt-get install python3-ijson`** in `sonic_debian_extension.j2`
- Installs Debian's `python3-ijson` (3.4.0) with the `yajl2_c` C extension **before** `sonic-yang-mgmt` is pip-installed
- This way pip sees "Requirement already satisfied" and doesn't download from PyPI

**3. Removed `ijson==3.2.3` from build constraint file** (`files/build/versions-public/host-image/versions-py3`)
- `sonic-build-hooks` intercepts all pip3 commands and injects `--constraint versions-py3`
- Even with `>=3.2.3` in setup.py and apt's 3.4.0 pre-installed, the constraint file forced pip to download and install 3.2.3 from PyPI, **replacing** apt's 3.4.0
- Removing `ijson==3.2.3` from the constraint file allows pip to accept the pre-installed 3.4.0

#### How to verify it

**Build log evidence** (from this PR's VS image build):
```
Line 722: Get:1 .../python3-ijson_3.4.0-1_amd64.deb  ← apt installs 3.4.0 with yajl2_c
Line 740: Requirement already satisfied: ijson>=3.2.3 in /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages (3.4.0)  ← pip accepts it!
```

Compare to **before** (without constraint file fix): `Downloading ijson-3.2.3.tar.gz` → pip replaced apt's 3.4.0 with pure-Python 3.2.3.

**KVM testbed verification:**
```
admin@sonic:~$ python3 -c "import ijson; print(ijson.backend)"
yajl2_c
admin@sonic:~$ python3 -c "import ijson; print(ijson.__file__)"
/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/ijson/__init__.py   ← Debian package, not pip
```

#### Companion PR
- **sonic-utilities PR**: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-utilities/pull/4436 (removes forced `IJSON_BACKEND=python` from route_check.py)
- ⚠️ **Merge order**: This buildimage PR must merge **first**, then the utilities PR. If reversed, images would lose the forced python backend while pip's ijson (without yajl2_c) is still installed.

#### Which release branch to backport
Master (and any branch where [sonic-utilities#4294](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-utilities/pull/4294) was cherry-picked)
